title: Emergent magnetic pseudogap from phase fluctuations and hierarchy of scales in two-dimensional superconductors
abstract: Preformed pairs and phase fluctuations are believed to play a vital role in predicting the charge pseudogap in the normal state of two-dimensional superconductors. In this work, we extend this idea and further identify the emergent magnetic pseudogap from pure phase fluctuations without invoking any competing order. We examine the NMR relaxation rate $1/T_1T$ by evaluating the bubble contribution and leading-order vertex correction within perturbation theory. It is found that the magnetic pseudogap, manifesting as a smooth suppression of $1/T_1T$ in the normal state, is characterized by a temperature scale $T_\text{mPG}$ distinct from the superconducting gap $Δ_\text{SC}$ and transition temperature $T_c$. The onset scales of both charge and magnetic pseudogap are dominated by the competition of BKT correlation length $ξ(T)$ and BCS coherence length $ξ_\text{BCS}$. Moreover, the vertex correction is shown to be irrelevant for $d$-wave pairing, while it becomes prominent in $s$-wave systems and drives a coherent enhancement of $1/T_1T$ at lower temperatures just above $T_c$. We attribute this normal-state enhancement of $1/T_1T$ to the diverging coherence peak at the $s$-wave superconducting gap edge, which shares the same spirit as the celebrated Hebel-Slichter peak in the BCS theory. Analogous to the coherent Hebel-Slichter peak, regularization by Fermi-liquid-like scatterings is important and is characterized by a scattering length $\ell$. The normal-state coherent enhancement of $1/T_1T$ is hence described by the competition of $ξ(T)$ and $\ell$, through which the coherence scale $T_\text{coh}$ is determined. As a result, the complete evolution of $1/T_1T$ is understood quantitatively in a unified picture as the interplay among hierarchy of scales $ξ(T)$, $ξ_\text{BCS}$ and $\ell$.
summary: This work theoretically predicts an emergent magnetic pseudogap in 2D superconductors arising purely from phase fluctuations. By analyzing the NMR relaxation rate (1/T1T), the authors show that the full temperature dependence is governed by a hierarchy of competing length scales: BKT correlations, BCS coherence, and background scattering. This provides a unified theoretical framework for understanding normal-state superconducting signatures.
main_problem: To theoretically identify an emergent magnetic pseudogap in two-dimensional superconductors arising purely from phase fluctuations, independent of invoking competing ordered states.
main_result: The paper establishes a unified picture where the normal-state spin relaxation rate (1/T1T) evolves based on the interplay between three characteristic length scales: the BKT correlation length ($\xi(T)$), the BCS coherence length ($\xi_{BCS}$), and an external scattering length ($\ell$).
method: The analysis uses perturbation theory applied to the NMR relaxation rate (1/T1T), calculating contributions from both bubble diagrams and leading-order vertex corrections.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D superconductors, modeled phenomenologically with a Hamiltonian incorporating spatially fluctuating superconducting order parameters ($\Delta(r, s)$). Comparisons are made between d-wave and s-wave pairing symmetries.
key_observables: NMR relaxation rate (1/T1T), charge pseudogap scale, magnetic pseudogap scale ($T_{mPG}$), and the coherence enhancement peak near $T_c$.
important_parameters: BKT correlation length $\xi(T)$, BCS coherence length $\xi_{BCS}$, background scattering length $\ell$, superconducting gap ($\Delta_{SC}$), and transition temperature ($T_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of treating static phase fluctuations near the BKT point, allowing for a perturbative expansion in terms of weak pairing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how characteristic scales like $\xi(T_{mPG})$ and $\xi(T_{coh})$ are determined by analyzing the derivatives or maxima of the calculated 1/T1T contributions with respect to varying length scale ratios.
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework for phase fluctuations, calculates the leading-order corrections to $1/T_1T$ (bubble and vertex), distinguishes behavior between d-wave and s-wave systems, and finally unifies these results by showing how all scales ($\xi(T)$, $\xi_{BCS}$, $\ell$) govern the full temperature evolution of $1/T_1T$.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of spectral function divergences (like the Hebel-Slichter peak) and their regularization via scattering lengths provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding how quantum fluctuations modify fundamental superconducting signatures, relevant to strongly correlated systems.
